notes: Sixteen newly authored five-part matching tasks with eighty exact-fragment suggested answers. NOT recovered board/school questions, official exercises or official keys. No PDF/source checksum, board, school or historical marks invented.

Each complete exercise has five A fragments, five independently shuffled B fragments and five independently shuffled C fragments. Zero-based answerPairs map each A row to one B and one C; every fragment is used once. Answers concatenate the exact displayed text. Teacher review should consider other semantically defensible readings instead of treating the suggested mapping as an official exclusive key.

Subjects overlap deliberately with the separately authored writing supplement across DIFFERENT task types. These are not additional original works, exam sources or recovered stock. Within matching they introduce distinct functional scenarios rather than repeat existing punctuality, morality, democracy, price-hike, generic education, Internet, Facebook, rights, water-pollution or greenhouse tables.

General safety, health, licensing, conservation and training-evaluation examples are educational language practice. No personalised clinical/legal advice, treatment dose, handling of hazards, guaranteed employment or guaranteed savings. Adult/qualified help where appropriate.

Authored status is always visible in instructions and draft names. No passage, sourceFile, boardSource or schoolSource is assigned. Existing board-year filters exclude these entries; Pending/explicit-consent/ADMIN review gate unchanged. No production import or approval.

rows: i. a borrowed book should be returned.

iv. the book’s place on the shelves.

subitems.answer: A library catalogue helps readers locate books by author, title or subject.

A loan record shows when a borrowed book should be returned.
If an item cannot be found, readers can ask a librarian for assistance.
